title: WHO physical activity guidance
text: For generally healthy adults, build activity gradually and combine aerobic movement with muscle-strengthening work. Some activity is better than none, and volume should reflect current ability.

title: WHO guidance for pregnancy and postpartum
text: Pregnancy and postpartum exercise recommendations depend on health status and contraindications. Use general guidance only after discussing individual circumstances with a qualified maternity-care professional.

title: NIH exercise and athletic-performance supplements
text: Supplement benefits and risks vary by ingredient, dose, health status, medications, and product quality. Food, training, and recovery fundamentals should come first; medication interactions require clinician or pharmacist review.

title: Squat setup principles
text: Use a stable stance, maintain pressure across the whole foot, brace the trunk, and let the knees track with the toes. Comfortable stance width, toe angle, and depth vary with anatomy, mobility, load, and goals.

title: Deadlift setup principles
text: Choose a load you can control, brace before lifting, keep the load close, and coordinate hip and knee extension without jerking. Stop the set when technique changes substantially or symptoms appear.

title: Recovery fundamentals
text: Recovery is supported by adequate sleep, regular nutrition, progressive training loads, and easier days. Mild delayed soreness can occur after unfamiliar work, but severe, worsening, or function-limiting symptoms need assessment.

title: Nutrition foundations
text: Sustainable nutrition starts with adequate energy, varied minimally processed foods, protein sources, fruits or vegetables, hydration, and changes that fit the person's culture, access, and preferences.

title: Progressive training principles
text: Begin with a manageable dose, practice consistent technique, and progress gradually by changing one variable such as repetitions, sets, load, range, or frequency. Include recovery based on performance and symptoms.
